text:
Matthew Wood is in the stretch every young scorer dreads. The 15th pick in 2023 out of UConn scored 17 goals in his first 77 NHL games, but this season he has one goal in 18 games and none in his last 10, and his ice time has slipped two minutes to about 13 a night.

Our numbers say the chances are still there. He has 3.4 expected goals (the quality of his shots) for one goal, a 4.3% shooting rate against a talent range around 13%, and that kind of gap usually closes. His own chance rate, 0.81 expected goals per 60, isn't far off last season's 0.91. The wider problem is the team around him: the Predators get 43% of the five-on-five shot attempts with him on the ice, though that's a little better than when he sits. Evolving-Hockey had him worth 1.4 wins last season, 110th among 401 forwards, and Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking had him as more of a setup man than his scoring reputation suggests, 8.2 primary shot assists per 60.
